question: Two addicts cannot resist the drug. One hates his craving; one welcomes it. On Frankfurt's view, who takes it freely?
answer: The one who welcomes it. In his 1971 paper Frankfurt calls the unwilling addict a helpless bystander to a desire he rejects. The willing addict would take the drug anyway, but he endorses the craving that moves him, so he takes it freely. Same craving, same drug: only one man is on its side.
move: Ask not only what someone wants, but whether they want to want it.
trap: Assuming no act can be free if it could not have been resisted.
reference: Frankfurt, Freedom of the Will and the Concept of a Person, Journal of Philosophy 68 (1), 1971
